Context: 2021 Ethiopian general election.

**Archived source account.** Ethiopian voters head to the polls to elect a new session to the House of Peoples' Representatives after months of delays. The election occurs in the midst of multiple problems affecting the country, such as the COVID-19 pandemic, deteriorating conditions in the Tigray Region brought on by the Tigray War, and the jailing of multiple oppositional figures.

Source citations (as archived): [CNN](<https://www.cnn.com/2021/06/21/africa/ethiopia-election-abiy-ahmed-cmd-intl/index.html>).

<a id="event-2021-06-21-3-4"></a>

**Archived source account.** The Australian National Party undergoes a leadership spill, replacing Michael McCormack with New England Representative Barnaby Joyce. Joyce previously lead the Nationals from 2016 to 2018 and was replaced by McCormack following sexual harassment allegations. As per the party's coalition agreement with the Australian Liberal Party, Joyce is set to replace McCormack as Deputy Prime Minister. Many Nationals have been critical of the Morrison Government's move towards carbon neutrality and hope that Joyce will counter this.

Source citations (as archived): [ABC News Australia](<https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-06-21/barnaby-joyce-wins-nationals-leadership-challenge/100230060>).

<a id="event-2021-06-23-2-1"></a>

Context: Russia–United Kingdom relations.

Context: China–United States relations.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/23/us-sanctions-chinese-solar-firms-for-uighur-human-rights-abuses>).

<a id="event-2021-06-23-2-4"></a>

**Archived source account.** The United Nations votes 184-2 on a resolution ending the embargo on Cuba, with the United States and Israel being the lone no votes.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/us-continues-vote-against-un-call-end-cuba-embargo-2021-06-23/>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2021-06-23-3-1"></a>

Context: Aftermath of the 2021 United States Capitol attack.

**Archived source account.** An Indiana woman is sentenced to three years probation for her role in the attack on the United States Capitol, making her the first person to be sentenced in the riot.

Source citations (as archived): [ABC News](<https://abcnews.go.com/US/im-ashamed-woman-breached-capitol-receives-probation-1st/story?id=78445859>).

<a id="event-2021-06-23-3-2"></a>

Context: Aftermath of the 2021 United States Capitol attack.

**Archived source account.** Graydon Young pleads guilty to conspiracy charges for his role in the Capitol riot, making him the first member of the Oath Keepers to do so.

Source citations (as archived): [NPR](<https://www.npr.org/2021/06/23/1009597270/first-guilty-plea-january-6-oath-keepers-conspiracy-case>).

<a id="event-2021-06-23-3-4"></a>

Context: Trial of Catalonia independence leaders.

**Archived source account.** The nine Catalan separatists pardoned on Tuesday leave prison after their pardons were ratified by King Felipe VI and after the Supreme Court set their imminent release.

Source citations (as archived): [RTVE](<https://www.rtve.es/noticias/20210623/lideres-del-proces-indultados-salen-prision-arropados-independentismo/2108680.shtml>).

<a id="event-2021-06-23-3-6"></a>

Context: Hong Kong national security law.

**Archived source account.** The pro-democracy newspaper Apple Daily announces that its final edition will be released on Thursday and that it will later cease activities after five top executives were arrested under the national security law and the newspaper's assets were frozen. Apple Daily founder Jimmy Lai is already imprisoned and awaits trial, along with 46 others, on subversion charges.

Source citations (as archived): [CNN](<https://edition.cnn.com/2021/06/23/media/apple-daily-closure-intl-hnk-dst/index.html>).

<a id="event-2021-06-23-3-8"></a>

Context: LGBT rights in Poland.

**Archived source account.** Polish education minister Przemysław Czarnek accuses the LGBT community of "insulting public morality" for a march held on Saturday in support of rights for the community. The opposition condemns Czarnek's comments as "language of hate".

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/polish-education-minister-says-lgbt-march-insult-public-morality-2021-06-23/>).

<a id="event-2021-06-23-3-9"></a>

**Archived source account.** American businessman John McAfee is found dead in his Barcelona prison cell, believed to be caused by suicide after the Spanish High Court authorized an extradition request for tax evasion earlier in the day.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/john-mcafee-found-dead-prison-after-spanish-court-allows-extradition-2021-06-23/>).

<a id="event-2021-06-23-3-10"></a>

**Archived source account.** The Cowessess First Nation and the Federation of Sovereign Indigenous Nations announce the discovery of hundreds of unmarked graves at the site of the former Marieval Indian Residential School in Saskatchewan, Canada.

Source citations (as archived): [CBC News](<https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/saskatchewan/cowessess-graves-unmarked-residential-school-marieval-1.6077797>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

Context: War in Afghanistan.

**Archived source account.** It is announced that around 650 American forces will remain in the country of Afghanistan to provide security for workers at the Kabul embassy after most troops withdraw from Afghanistan.

Source citations (as archived): [Politico](<https://www.politico.com/news/2021/06/24/us-troops-afghanistan-withdrawl-496137>).

#### Arts and culture

<a id="event-2021-06-24-1-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences announces that American actors Samuel L. Jackson and Danny Glover, American writer and director Elaine May, and Norwegian actress Liv Ullmann are the next recipients of the Governors Awards for their lifetime contributions to filmmaking.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/world/us/samuel-l-jackson-danny-glover-receive-honorary-oscars-2021-06-24/>).

#### Business and economy

<a id="event-2021-06-24-2-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** UK Public Health Minister Jo Churchill announces that junk food advertisements during daytime television and on the internet will be banned in the United Kingdom by the end of the year, saying it will help fight the growing rates of childhood obesity in the country.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/uk-ban-daytime-junk-food-adverts-tv-online-2021-06-24/>).

#### Disasters and accidents

<a id="event-2021-06-24-3-1"></a>

Context: Surfside condominium building collapse.

**Archived source account.** A 12-story condominium in Surfside, Florida, U.S., partially collapses overnight, killing ninety-eight people and injuring eleven others.

<a id="event-2021-06-24-3-3"></a>

Context: 2021 South Moravia tornado.

**Archived source account.** A rare powerful tornado passes through several villages in southeastern Czech Republic, causing catastrophic damage. Much of Hrušky has been destroyed, according to its mayor. Five people are killed and 150 others are injured. Rescue teams from neighbouring Austria and Slovakia have been deployed to the region.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-57605651>).

#### Health and environment

<a id="event-2021-06-24-4-3"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal.

**Archived source account.** Portuguese authorities announce that restaurants and non-food shops in Albufeira, Lisbon and Sesimbra will close on weekends at 3:30 p.m. while supermarkets and other food outlets will close on weekends at 7:00 p.m. as part of measures to reduce the spread of COVID-19 in the region.

Source citations (as archived): [Bloomberg](<https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-06-24/portugal-says-lisbon-stores-will-close-earlier-during-weekends>); [The Portugal News](<https://www.theportugalnews.com/news/2021-06-24/albufeira-and-lisbon-take-a-step-backwards-in-the-easing-of-lockdown/60658>).

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in Russia.

**Archived source account.** Russia reports 20,182 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, which is the highest single-day total of new cases since January, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 5.38 million.

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom.

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji.

**Archived source account.** Fiji reports a record for the third consecutive day of 308 new cases of COVID-19, thereby bringing the national total to 2,848 cases. The Ministry of Health reports that Australia is helping with the supply of vaccines.

Source citations (as archived): [RNZ](<https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/445459/it-s-too-early-for-covid-19-to-be-endemic-fiji-govt>).

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji.

**Archived source account.** Despite continuous records of new cases, the government rules out any possibility of a nationwide lockdown, adding that their directive would be on targeted lockdowns instead.

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji.

**Archived source account.** The Fiji Ministry of Health reports that more than 260,000 Fijians have received their first dose of the Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine, equivalent to 45% of the target population, and that 27,000 Fijians have already received both doses of the vaccine.

<a id="event-2021-06-24-4-16"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia.

**Archived source account.** Indonesia reports a record 20,574 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, 7,505 of which are from Jakarta, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2.05 million.

#### International relations

<a id="event-2021-06-24-5-1"></a>

Context: Russia–United Kingdom relations.

**Archived source account.** Russia warns the United Kingdom that it will bomb British vessels if any further provocative action is taken by the British Royal Navy in the Black Sea. Russia had previously summoned the British ambassador to Russia over this week's incident. The UK says that the vessel was in Ukrainian waters, that it was entirely right to use the route, and that the Royal Navy will always uphold international law and will not accept unlawful interference with innocent passage.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/britain-says-dont-get-carried-away-by-warship-spat-with-russia-2021-06-24/>).

<a id="event-2021-06-24-5-3"></a>

Context: Foreign relations of Hungary, LGBT rights in Hungary.

**Archived source account.** Dutch Prime Minister Mark Rutte says that Hungary "has no business being in the European Union any more" following the approval of an anti-pedophilia law in Hungary, which is claimed by some critics to also contain anti-LGBT parts. Rutte says that he cannot push Hungary out of the European Union but that it has to be done step by step until Hungary is brought "to its knees on this issue".

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-57596263>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2021-06-24-6-2"></a>

Context: Aftermath of the January 6 United States Capitol attack / January 6 commission, United States House Select Committee on the January 6 Attack.

**Archived source account.** U.S. House Speaker Nancy Pelosi announces that the House will create a select committee to investigate the January 6 riot at the United States Capitol.

Source citations (as archived): [NBC News](<https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/pelosi-announces-select-committee-investigate-jan-6-capitol-riot-n1272252>).

<a id="event-2021-06-24-6-3"></a>

Context: Aftermath of the January 6 United States Capitol attack.

**Archived source account.** United States Attorney General Merrick Garland announces that over 500 people have been arrested for their role in the Capitol riot, including 100 for assaulting Capitol Police officers. Garland also announces that the Department of Justice has arrested the first suspect involved in assaulting media reporters during the events of January 6.

Source citations (as archived): [Forbes](<https://www.forbes.com/sites/andrewsolender/2021/06/24/100-arrested-on-charges-of-assaulting-police-in-capitol-riot-attorney-general-says/?sh=14c633481cd5>).

<a id="event-2021-06-24-6-5"></a>

Context: 2021 Canadian Indian residential schools gravesite discoveries.

**Archived source account.** The discovery of 751 unmarked graves at the site of Marieval Indian Residential School in Saskatchewan, Canada, is announced, weeks after the remains of 215 children were found at a similar residential school in British Columbia.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-57592243>).

<a id="event-2021-06-24-6-7"></a>

Context: Hong Kong national security law.

**Archived source account.** The pro-democracy tabloid Apple Daily ceases its activities due to the national security law and after five of its top executives as well as its founder Jimmy Lai were arrested for violating that law. Thousands of Hong Kong residents purchase the tabloid's final edition and a million copies were printed as critics say that a different era begins for Hong Kong given the unapologetic gesture of the Hong Kong government regarding the closure of the tabloid.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/jun/24/hong-kong-apple-daily-queue-final-edition-newspaper>).

<a id="event-2021-06-24-6-9"></a>

Context: 2020–2021 Thai protests.

**Archived source account.** Pro-democracy protests resume in Thailand despite COVID-19 restrictions. Protesters demand the resignation of Prime Minister Prayut Chan-o-cha over his alleged mishandling of the COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand and other issues such as monarchy and government reforms.

Source citations (as archived): [DW](<https://www.dw.com/en/thai-protesters-return-to-the-streets-despite-covid-concerns/a-58027050>).

<a id="event-2021-06-24-6-11"></a>

Context: Belarusian democracy movement.

**Archived source account.** The trial of Belarusian activist Sergei Tikhanovsky begins in Belarus. Tikhanovsky faces charges of inciting the protests against the government of Alexander Lukashenko and could face up to 15 years' imprisonment.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/world/belarus-starts-trial-opposition-leader-tsikhanouskayas-husband-2021-06-24/>).

<a id="event-2021-06-24-6-12"></a>

**Archived source account.** Gilmar Mendes, a magistrate judge on the Supreme Federal Court, overturns two cases brought by former federal judge Sergio Moro against former Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

Source citations (as archived): [Buenos Aires Times](<https://www.batimes.com.ar/news/latin-america/brazil-judge-annuls-all-of-moros-cases-against-ex-president-lula.phtml>).

<a id="event-2021-06-24-6-13"></a>

**Archived source account.** Sri Lankan President Gotabaya Rajapaksa pardons 16 Tamil Tigers members, with government officials saying that it is the start of a process to gradually free all individuals who have been charged under the Prevention of Terrorism Act.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/24/sri-lanka-pardons-suspected-tamil-tigers-convicted-of-terrorism>).

The protestors called for the government, and current President Mahmoud Abbas in particular, to be "overthrown".

<a id="event-2021-06-25-5-1"></a>

Context: 2021 Gibraltar abortion referendum.

**Archived source account.** Gibraltar votes 62% in favour of legalizing abortion. Under the new proposed amendment to the criminal law bill, pregnancies can be terminated by a registered physician within the first 12 weeks, while abortions would be permitted at a later stage of the pregnancy under a "narrow set of circumstances".

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/world/gibraltar-approves-easing-strict-abortion-law-referendum-2021-06-25/>).

<a id="event-2021-06-25-5-2"></a>

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2021-06-28-5-1"></a>

Context: 2021 Samoan constitutional crisis.

**Archived source account.** The Supreme Court of Samoa rules that the swearing in of the FAST party-led government on May 24th was illegal. However, the court also orders that the Legislative Assembly of Samoa sit within seven days, giving the opposition FAST, led by Naomi Mataʻafa, the ability to form a new government. FAST currently holds 26 seats in parliament, while the caretaker HRPP government of Tuila'epa Sa'ilele Malielegaoi has 24 seats.

Source citations (as archived): [RNZI](<https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/445660/samoa-s-parliament-ordered-to-sit-within-a-week>).

Context: Personal and business legal affairs of Donald Trump.

Source citations (as archived): [The New York Times](<https://www.nytimes.com/2021/06/30/nyregion/trump-organization-cfo-allen-weisselberg.html>).

<a id="event-2021-06-30-5-13"></a>

Context: LGBTQ rights in the United States.

**Archived source account.** U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken announces that the U.S. passport will include an option for a third gender, and that effective immediately, applicants can indicate their gender without having to provide medical proof.

Source citations (as archived): [NPR](<https://www.npr.org/2021/06/30/1011866915/u-s-will-add-an-option-other-than-male-or-female-on-passports>).

<a id="event-2021-06-30-5-14"></a>

**Archived source account.** Saudi Arabian state-run news channel Al Arabiya reports that authorities seized a shipment of 4.5 million Captagon amphetamine pills, smuggled inside several orange cartons, at a port in Jeddah.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/30/saudi-arabia-seizes-4-5m-amphetamine-pills-hidden-in-oranges>).

<a id="event-2021-06-30-5-15"></a>

**Archived source account.** The UN International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals sentences both Serbian State Security Service chief Jovica Stanišić and his deputy Franko "Frenki" Simatović to 12 years in prison for providing support to Serb paramilitary groups that carried out ethnic cleansings against the Croat and Bosniak populations in the Bosnian town of Šamac during the Bosnian War. The case against the two men was the longest international war crime case in history, having started in 2003, and marks the first time that senior officials in the government of former Serbian President Slobodan Milošević were convicted for war crimes committed during the war.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/law/2021/jun/30/serbian-secret-police-jovica-stanisic-franko-simatovic-sentenced-atrocities-bosnian-war-hague>).

<a id="event-2021-06-30-5-16"></a>

**Archived source account.** On the 32nd anniversary of the 1989 Sudanese coup d'état, Sudanese authorities arrest at least 200 members of deposed Sudanese President Omar al-Bashir's National Congress Party in the early morning for allegedly promoting instability.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/sudan-arrests-scores-former-ruling-party-members-before-protests-2021-06-30/>).

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2021-06-30-6-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** President of Algeria Abdelmadjid Tebboune appoints Minister of Finance Aymen Benabderrahmane as the new Prime Minister.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/30/algeria-names-finance-chief-benabderrahmane-as-prime-minister>).

<a id="event-2021-06-30-6-1"></a>

**Archived source account.** Hundreds of protestors march in the Sudanese capital of Khartoum and call for the resignation of the transitional government after the government reduced bread and fuel subsidies in order to fulfill its obligations with the International Monetary Fund.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/30/sudan-protesters-demand-govt-step-down-over-imf-backed-reforms>).

#### Sports

<a id="event-2021-06-30-7-1"></a>

Context: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports, COVID-19 vaccine.

**Archived source account.** Japanese Prime Minister Yoshihide Suga pledges help to the Cook Islands, the Marshall Islands, the Federated States of Micronesia, Niue and Tonga to strengthen their health systems while vowing to the leaders of those nations to host a "safe and secure" 2020 Summer Olympics.

Source citations (as archived): [Kyodo News](<https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2021/06/87dc6f8ee663-suga-vows-covid-19-support-for-pacific-islands-in-online-meetings.html>).

<a id="event-2021-06-30-7-3"></a>

Context: 2021 College World Series.

**Archived source account.** In college baseball, the Mississippi State Bulldogs win the College World Series for the first time in their 126-year history following a 9-0 victory against the Vanderbilt Commodores.

Source citations (as archived): [ESPN](<https://www.espn.com/college-sports/story/_/id/31740978/college-world-series-2021-mississippi-state-ends-126-year-title-drought>).

<a id="event-2021-06-30-7-4"></a>

**Archived source account.** The Court of Arbitration for Sport bans Bahraini 400 m-runner Salwa Eid Naser from participating in the sport for two years, thus banning her from the Tokyo Olympics, for not taking doping tests between March 2019 and January 2020. This overturns the ruling made by the World Athletics Disciplinary Tribunal last October, who absolved her based on a technicality.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/30/bahraini-world-champion-sprinter-naser-gets-two-year-doping-ban>).

<a id="event-2021-06-30-7-5"></a>

**Archived source account.** American chess player Abhimanyu Mishra becomes the youngest Grandmaster (GM) in the world, at age 12, after defeating Indian GM Leon Luke Mendonca in Budapest.

Source citations (as archived): [ESPN](<https://www.espn.com/chess/story/_/id/31738870/american-abhimanyu-mishra-becomes-youngest-grandmaster-chess-history>).


## July

### 2021-07-01

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1101112168](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2021%20July%201&oldid=1101112168>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2021-07-01-0-1"></a>

Context: Allied Democratic Forces insurgency.

**Archived source account.** Authorities reveal that the attackers who attempted to assassinate Ugandan general Katumba Wamala in Kampala were Islamic extremists who were trained in a jihadist camp in North Kivu, Democratic Republic of Congo, and had links with the Allied Democratic Forces and the Islamic State. Wamala was injured during the attack but survived, while his daughter and his driver were killed.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/uganda-links-islamist-rebels-attempted-murder-minister-2021-07-01/>).

<a id="event-2021-07-01-0-2"></a>

Context: Allied Democratic Forces insurgency.

**Archived source account.** U.S. Ambassador to the Democratic Republic of the Congo Michael A. Hammer announces that the U.S. government will assist in training Congolese forces and with intelligence sharing.

Source citations (as archived): [Newsweek](<https://www.newsweek.com/us-sending-soldiers-congo-train-army-help-find-rebels-who-killed-9-attack-1606072>).

#### Arts and culture

<a id="event-2021-07-01-1-1"></a>

Context: 2021 Canadian Indian residential schools gravesite discoveries.

**Archived source account.** Indigenous protesters tear down the Statue of Queen Victoria in Winnipeg, Manitoba, Canada, as protests grow over the mass graves of indigenous children discovered at former Canadian Indian residential schools. A smaller statue of Queen Elizabeth II was also toppled nearby. Multiple Catholic Churches on or near indigenous grounds have been burned down.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-57693683>); [CBC](<https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/edmonton/morinville-church-alberta-burned-fire-1.6085688>).

#### Business and economy

<a id="event-2021-07-01-2-1"></a>

Context: Economy of El Salvador.

**Archived source account.** President Nayib Bukele requests a minimum wage increase of 20% due to poor Salvadorans suffering from an "onslaught of global inflation". Bukele also orders more food handouts to combat hunger during the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic. The country recently had a government reshuffle, which has put in doubt negotiations for a potential $1 billion financing program from the International Monetary Fund.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/el-salvadors-bukele-seeks-20-minimum-wage-hike-orders-food-handouts-2021-07-01/>).

<a id="event-2021-07-01-2-3"></a>

Context: Economy of Uganda.

**Archived source account.** Uganda imposes a new tax rate for using the internet as the government orders a 12% excise duty on mobile data. President Yoweri Museveni defends the tax as he says that social media users are "endlessly donating money to foreign telephone companies through chatting or even lying" and described the use of social media as a "luxury". This tax proposal, which takes effect immediately, resulted in protests in 2018 and 2019.

Source citations (as archived): [Africa Feeds](<https://africafeeds.com/2021/07/01/ugandans-paying-new-tax-for-using-the-internet/>).

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2021-07-01-3-1"></a>

Context: Politics of China.

**Archived source account.** CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping delivered a speech in which he specifically announced the realization of the first goal of the Two Centenaries goal set.

Source citations (as archived): [The New York Times](<https://www.nytimes.com/live/2021/06/30/world/china-communist-party-anniversary>).

#### Disasters and accidents

<a id="event-2021-07-01-4-1"></a>

Context: 2021 Madagascar food crisis.

**Archived source account.** UN agencies report that due to the food insecurity that has affected around one million people in Madagascar, the population has been surviving by eating ashes mixed with tamarind and shoe leather, as the United States and South Korea pledge economic aid to Malagasy President Andry Rajoelina.

Source citations (as archived): [Metro UK](<https://metro.co.uk/2021/07/01/starving-people-in-madagascar-eating-ash-during-worst-drought-in-decades-14858844/>).

<a id="event-2021-07-01-4-4"></a>

Context: 2021 Western North America heat wave / Lytton wildfire.

**Archived source account.** The village of Lytton, British Columbia, is evacuated after a wildfire destroys 90% of the village amid an unprecedented heat wave caused by a rare "heat dome" event over the Pacific Northwest and Western Canada. The village recently recorded Canada's highest ever temperature of 49.6 C.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-57678054>).

<a id="event-2021-07-01-4-6"></a>

Context: 2020–2021 Taal Volcano eruptions.

**Archived source account.** The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) raises the alert status of Taal Volcano to level 3 after the volcano emitted a kilometer-high ash plume, forcing authorities in the provinces of Batangas and Cavite to evacuate thousands of people.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/1/evacuation-under-way-as-philippines-raises-volcano-danger-level>).

#### Health and environment

<a id="event-2021-07-01-5-3"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Asia / COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh.

**Archived source account.** Bangladesh imposes a lockdown that suspends all public transport and only allows people to leave their house for emergency reasons due to a substantial increase in the number of COVID-19 cases. Soldiers are deployed to enforce the lockdown.

Source citations (as archived): [Voice of America](<https://www.voanews.com/covid-19-pandemic/bangladesh-lock-down-covid-19-cases-surge>).

<a id="event-2021-07-01-5-6"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Asia / COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia / Community Activities Restrictions Enforcement.

**Archived source account.** President Joko Widodo announces emergency community restrictions in 122 regencies and cities in Java and Bali, including the capital Jakarta from July 3 to 20 which would require non-essential businesses and places of worship to close.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/indonesia-emergency-covid-19-curbs-be-effective-july-2-20-minister-2021-07-01/>); [CNA](<https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/indonesia-covid-19-emergency-restrictions-ppkm-java-bali-15115348>).

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Asia / COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia.

**Archived source account.** Indonesia reports a record 24,836 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2.2 million.

Source citations (as archived): [detikNews](<https://news.detik.com/berita/d-5627352/24836-kasus-baru-hari-ini-rekor-tertinggi-sepanjang-sejarah-corona-ri>).

<a id="event-2021-07-01-5-9"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Asia / COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand.

**Archived source account.** Thailand reports a record 57 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 2,080.

Source citations (as archived): [Bangkok Post](<https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2141591/record-57-covid-deaths-5-533-new-cases>).

<a id="event-2021-07-01-5-12"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in Russia.

**Archived source account.** Russia reports a record for the third consecutive day of 672 deaths from COVID-19, bringing the nationwide death toll to 135,886.

Source citations (as archived): [The Moscow Times](<https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2021/07/01/russia-posts-record-covid-deaths-for-third-day-running-a74385>).

<a id="event-2021-07-01-5-14"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey.

**Archived source account.** Turkey lifts nearly all COVID-19-related business restrictions, as well as nighttime and Sunday curfews as the number of cases remains steady. Only hookah shops continue to remain closed.

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<https://apnews.com/article/middle-east-europe-turkey-pandemics-lifestyle-b95a3b1c535f6d2d413dbdf147208e72>).

<a id="event-2021-07-01-5-16"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey / COVID-19 vaccination in Turkey.

**Archived source account.** Turkey begins to give a third dose of the COVID-19 vaccine to healthcare workers and people aged above 50 years old.

Source citations (as archived): [Hurriyet Daily News](<https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkey-starts-giving-third-dose-of-covid-19-vaccine-165950>).

<a id="event-2021-07-01-5-18"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom.

**Archived source account.** The United Kingdom reports 27,989 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, which is the highest single-day total of cases since January 25.

Source citations (as archived): [ITV News](<https://www.itv.com/news/2021-07-01/uk-records-27989-covid-cases-highest-since-january-25-and-fourth-day-in-a-row-of-more-than-20000-positive-tests>).

<a id="event-2021-07-01-5-19"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe.

**Archived source account.** The European Union launches the EU Digital COVID Certificate that contains a proof of vaccination, a negative test, or proof of recovery from COVID-19, and is designed to allow Europeans to resume travel across the bloc without quarantine in order to boost tourism.

Source citations (as archived): [Financial Times](<https://www.ft.com/content/7d48a006-cdfa-4b27-a663-21428471fbc5>).

<a id="event-2021-07-01-5-21"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji.

**Archived source account.** Fiji reports a record of 431 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the national total of cases to 4,849. The Ministry of Health and Medical Services also reports two deaths, bringing the death toll to 24, with 22 of these deaths having occurred since the current outbreak began in April.

Source citations (as archived): [RNZ](<https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/445969/fiji-covid-19-431-new-cases-and-two-deaths>).

<a id="event-2021-07-01-5-25"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in the United States / COVID-19 vaccination in the United States / COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan.

**Archived source account.** Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer announces a month-long vaccination raffle in which residents can win a total of $5 million in cash (one grand prize of $2 million or three prizes of $1 million) and $500,000 total in college scholarships for children aged 12 to 17 years old (nine prizes of $55,000). The winners will be drawn on August 4.

Source citations (as archived): [MLive.com](<https://www.mlive.com/public-interest/2021/07/nearly-500k-residents-have-signed-up-for-michigans-vaccine-lottery.html>).

<a id="event-2021-07-01-5-27"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Sierra Leone.

**Archived source account.** President Julius Maada Bio announces a nationwide curfew in the country to combat the spread of COVID-19.

Source citations (as archived): [The Sierra Leone Telegraph](<https://www.thesierraleonetelegraph.com/president-bio-announces-new-measures-to-curb-rising-covid-cases-and-deaths-in-sierra-leone/>).

#### International relations

<a id="event-2021-07-01-6-1"></a>

Context: Turkey–United States relations.

**Archived source account.** The United States adds Turkey to its list of governments that are implicated in the use of child soldiers, saying that the country has provided "tangible support" to the Neo-Ottoman Sultan Murad Division, in Syria and Libya, which uses child soldiers. It is the first time that a NATO member state has been included in the Trafficking in Persons Report.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/us-adds-turkey-list-countries-implicated-use-child-soldiers-2021-07-01/>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2021-07-01-7-1"></a>

Context: Cannabis in Rwanda.

**Archived source account.** Rwanda legalizes the medical use of cannabis. However, recreational use of cannabis remains illegal.

Source citations (as archived): [The East African](<https://www.theeastafrican.co.ke/tea/news/east-africa/rwanda-legalises-medical-use-of-cannabis--3456728>).

#### Science and technology

<a id="event-2021-07-01-8-1"></a>

Context: Climate change in Antarctica.

**Archived source account.** The United Nations' World Meteorological Organization confirms that a record high temperature of 18.3 °C (64.9 °F) has been recorded in Antarctica at the Esperanza Base.

Source citations (as archived): [France 24](<https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210701-un-confirms-18-3c-record-heat-in-antarctica>).

### 2021-07-02

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1262042905](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2021%20July%202&oldid=1262042905>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2021-07-02-0-2"></a>

Context: War in Afghanistan / Withdrawal of United States troops from Afghanistan; Taliban insurgency.

**Archived source account.** Bagram Airfield is looted by locals following the sudden American withdrawal from the airbase, which was conducted without notifying local forces. Afghan troops later cleared the airbase of looters and secured control of it.

Source citations (as archived): [Newsweek](<https://www.newsweek.com/looters-moved-afghanistans-bagram-airfield-hours-after-us-troops-left-1606385>).

<a id="event-2021-07-02-0-3"></a>

Context: War in Afghanistan / Withdrawal of United States troops from Afghanistan; Taliban insurgency.

**Archived source account.** Pentagon spokesperson John Kirby announces that U.S. Defense Secretary Lloyd Austin has approved a new command to oversee troops who will remain in the country to protect diplomats at the U.S. Embassy in Kabul. The mission will be led by RDML Peter Vasely.

Source citations (as archived): [Stars and Stripes](<https://www.stripes.com/theaters/middle_east/2021-07-02/us-drawdown-afghanistan-mckenzie-miller-vasely-troops-2033972.html>).

<a id="event-2021-07-02-0-4"></a>

Context: War in Afghanistan / Withdrawal of United States troops from Afghanistan; Taliban insurgency.

**Archived source account.** It is reported that, during June, the Taliban captured 700 Humvees as well as dozens of armored vehicles and artillery systems from the Afghan National Army as more districts fall under the group's control during their offensive in the north.

Source citations (as archived): [Times of India](<https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/south-asia/afghanistan-taliban-captured-700-military-vehicles-as-fighting-intensifies/articleshow/84073763.cms>).

<a id="event-2021-07-02-1-1"></a>

Context: Transair Flight 810.

**Archived source account.** Transair Flight 810, a cargo flight from Honolulu to Kahului, ditches off the coast of Oahu. The two pilots are injured.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-57697835>).

<a id="event-2021-07-02-1-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** A massive fire breaks out at an undersea gas pipeline which connects to the Ku-Maloob-Zaap oil field, off the coast of the Yucatán Peninsula. The fire took five hours to contain. Mexican state-run oil company Pemex, who is in charge of the oil field's operations, orders an investigation into the cause of the fire.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/fire-offshore-pemex-platform-gulf-mexico-under-control-2021-07-02/>).

<a id="event-2021-07-02-3-1"></a>

Context: European migrant crisis, Belarus–Lithuania relations.

**Archived source account.** Lithuania declares a state of emergency amid an increase in the number of undocumented migrants crossing into the country from neighbouring Belarus. The Government of Lithuania accuses Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko of deliberately trying to destabilize the country by encouraging and allowing refugees, mostly Syrians, to cross the border.

Source citations (as archived): [Politico](<https://www.politico.eu/article/lithuania-state-emergency-migrants-belarus-border/>).

<a id="event-2021-07-02-3-3"></a>

Context: Belarus–Ukraine relations.

**Archived source account.** Belarus closes its border with Ukraine after President Alexander Lukashenko claims that arms are being smuggled into the country in an attempt by "outside powers" to overthrow his regime, saying that "They have crossed the line. We cannot forgive them". Ukraine denies Lukashenko's claims, and says that closing the border would make its people "suffer".

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-57702516>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

Context: War in Afghanistan / Taliban insurgency.

**Archived source account.** The Taliban takes control of several further districts overnight as Afghan troops abandon their posts and flee into neighboring Tajikistan via Badakhshan Province. The State Committee for National Security of Tajikistan reports that more than 300 Afghan troops crossed the Tajik border as Taliban spokesperson Zabiullah Mujahid confirms that most of the territory was gained without a fight.

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<https://apnews.com/article/joe-biden-taliban-afghanistan-a554e1731c767b5ffaf09fb98c81bc7e>).

<a id="event-2021-07-04-0-4"></a>

Context: War in Afghanistan / Withdrawal of United States troops from Afghanistan.

**Archived source account.** Taliban spokesperson Suhail Shaheen warns that all foreign troops must leave Afghanistan before a NATO deadline on September 11 amid reports that the U.S. military plans to keep 1,000 troops in Kabul in order to protect both its embassy and the Hamid Karzai International Airport.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-57714808>).

<a id="event-2021-07-04-0-6"></a>

**Archived source account.** Four Malian soldiers are killed in an ambush on their patrol. No group claims responsibility for the attack, which comes as France resumes joint military exercises with members of the Malian Armed Forces, which had been suspended following the coup d'état this year led by Colonel Assimi Goïta.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/mali-says-four-soldiers-killed-ambush-by-suspected-militants-2021-07-04/>).

<a id="event-2021-07-07-3-1"></a>

Context: Political impact of the COVID-19 pandemic.

**Archived source account.** Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi dismisses 12 cabinet ministers, including Health Minister Harsh Vardhan, following intense criticisms over his handling of the COVID-19 pandemic. Ravi Shankar Prasad, who held multiple concurrent positions as Law, Information Technology, and Communications Minister, also resigns.

Source citations (as archived): [South China Morning Post](<https://www.scmp.com/news/asia/south-asia/article/3140229/indias-modi-reshuffles-cabinet-amid-drop-popularity-during>).

<a id="event-2021-07-07-3-3"></a>

Context: Political impact of the COVID-19 pandemic / 2020–21 Malaysian political crisis.

**Archived source account.** The United Malays National Organisation (UMNO), the largest party in the ruling Perikatan Nasional coalition, withdraws its support for Malaysian Prime Minister Muhyiddin Yassin and calls for his resignation. The move occurred despite Yassin appointing UMNO vice-president Ismail Sabri Yaakob as Deputy Prime Minister and major party stalwart Hishammuddin Hussein as Senior Security Minister earlier in the day in order to prevent this. UMNO president Ahmad Zahid Hamidi says that the decision was due to Yassin's poor handling of the COVID-19 pandemic, with Hamidi specifically singling out the ineffective and contradictory implementation of the lockdowns as the main point of contention.

Source citations (as archived): [The Straits Times](<https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/umno-withdraws-support-for-malaysias-pm-muhyiddin-calls-for-his-resignation>); [South China Morning Post](<https://www.scmp.com/week-asia/politics/article/3140197/malaysias-prime-minister-muhyiddin-appoints-umno-stalwart-ismail>).

#### International relations

<a id="event-2021-07-08-3-1"></a>

Context: China–European Union relations.

The resolution also calls for the European Commission to take punitive actions in response, such as sanctioning officials responsible for drafting and enforcing the national security law, and refusing invitations to the Beijing Winter Olympics next year.

Source citations (as archived): [South China Morning Post](<https://www.scmp.com/news/china/diplomacy/article/3140391/european-parliament-adopts-resolution-hong-kong-press-freedom?module=lead_hero_story_2&amp;pgtype=homepage>).

The Bolivian government also accuses former president of Argentina Mauricio Macri of wanting the assassination of Evo Morales during his ousting. Argentina was among the first countries to recognize the interim presidency of Jeanine Áñez in 2019.

Source citations (as archived): [A24](<https://www.a24.com/politica/bolivia-denuncia-que-mauricio-macri-apoyo-el-golpe-estado-ese-pais-equipamiento-n845798>).

<a id="event-2021-07-09-1-2"></a>

Context: War in Afghanistan / Taliban insurgency / 2021 Taliban offensive.

**Archived source account.** The Taliban claims to have captured the strategic city of Spin Boldak, Kandahar Province, on the border with Pakistan. #### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2021-07-16-0-3"></a>

Context: War in Afghanistan / Taliban insurgency / 2021 Taliban offensive.

A senior Afghan officer is also killed in the attack. Reuters president Michael Friedenberg and editor-in-chief Alessandra Galloni say that they are urgently seeking information with authorities in the region. Reports by the government indicate that Siddiqui was killed in Taliban crossfire.

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom / COVID-19 pandemic in England.

**Archived source account.** Most legal restrictions on social contact are ended in England. Face coverings in indoor public places are no longer required by law, though they are still recommended in some settings. There are no more limits on how many people can attend events, nightclubs can reopen and table service will not be necessary in pubs and restaurants. People working from home as a result of the pandemic are formally encouraged to return to their workplace.

<a id="event-2021-07-19-2-24"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Europe / COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom / COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland.

**Archived source account.** Restrictions are also being eased across Scotland to level zero. Unlike in England, face coverings are still mandatory in indoor public places and on public transport. The change also means that four households can meet indoors at home, up to 10 households can meet in a pub or restaurant, up to 15 households can meet outdoors and up to 200 people can attend a wedding or funeral.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-57878745>).

The accusation comes as the National Jury of Elections says that it will announce the winner later this week, and dismissed five challenges to the results brought last week by the FP party.

Source citations (as archived): [U.S. News](<https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2021-07-19/perus-fujimori-admits-defeat-in-presidential-election-lashes-out-at-socialist-rival>); [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/peru-electoral-authority-cusp-confirming-new-president-scraps-last-fujimori-2021-07-19/>).

#### Science and technology

<a id="event-2021-07-19-6-1"></a>

Context: Project Pegasus revelations.

**Archived source account.** A consortium of journalists led by NGOs Forbidden Stories and Amnesty International reveal widespread spying abuses on journalists, political opposition, businesspeople, human rights activists and others by various governments under the guise of fighting crime or terrorism. The NGOs accessed a list of over 50,000 individuals targeted by Israeli security and spying software company NSO Group and its customers within 50 countries.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/news/series/pegasus-project>); [ForbiddenStories](<https://forbiddenstories.org/about-the-pegasus-project/>).

<a id="event-2021-07-19-6-2"></a>

Context: Project Pegasus revelations.

**Archived source account.** According to the leaked data, NSO Group's Pegasus spyware was used to target Saudi-American journalist Jamal Khashoggi and his family and friends in the months before and after Khashoggi's killing. Khashoggi was assassinated and dismembered in Saudi Arabia's embassy in Istanbul in 2018 by Saudi operatives. NSO previously denied any implication in the killing.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/jul/18/nso-spyware-used-to-target-family-of-jamal-khashoggi-leaked-data-shows-saudis-pegasus>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2021-07-22-3-1"></a>

Context: Asylum in Australia.

**Archived source account.** An Afghan Tajik asylum seeker who has been held in immigration detention by Australia for eight years sues the Australian Government in the Federal Court. A former employee of the Islamic Republican government, the man fled an assassination attempt by the Taliban and argues that his family is still being targeted in Afghanistan and that his indefinite detention prevents him from organising their escape from the violence. The Government has requested the case be dismissed and denied they had any legal obligations towards Afghan citizens.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/jul/22/afghan-refugee-sues-australian-government-saying-detention-prevents-him-saving-his-family-from-taliban>).

<a id="event-2021-07-22-3-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** Police in Madagascar arrest six individuals, including a foreign national, after months of investigation into a plot to kill President Andry Rajoelina. The Attorney General accuses those arrested of having "a plan for the elimination of the head of state".

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/several-arrested-over-plot-kill-madagascar-president-attorney-general-says-2021-07-22/>); [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/22/madagascar-says-foiled-plot-kill-president-andry-rajoelina>).

<a id="event-2021-07-22-3-3"></a>

**Archived source account.** Tanzanian opposition leader Freeman Mbowe and 15 members of his Chadema party, who were arrested yesterday, are charged with terrorism, according to a statement from the party. Amnesty International condemns the charges and the United States said yesterday that Mbowe's arrest was "very concerning".

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/22/tanzanian-opposition-leader-to-face-terrorism-charges-party>).

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2021-07-22-4-1"></a>

Context: 2021 Brazilian military crisis, 2022 Brazilian general election.

**Archived source account.** It is revealed that Brazilian Minister of Defence Braga Netto communicated to President of the Chamber of Deputies Arthur Lira that the 2022 elections would not be held if a controversial bill that bans electronic voting and reinstates the use of paper ballots does not pass through Congress. This report follows similar threats made by President Jair Bolsonaro, whose approval ratings and chances of re-election are continuing to decrease.

Source citations (as archived): [O Estado de S. Paulo](<https://politica.estadao.com.br/noticias/geral,ministro-da-defesa-faz-ameaca-e-condiciona-eleicoes-de-2022-ao-voto-impresso,70003785916>).

<a id="event-2021-07-22-4-2"></a>

Context: 2021 Brazilian military crisis, 2022 Brazilian general election.

**Archived source account.** Both Netto and Lira deny that such a threat happened, with the former declaring that the Estadão reported an "invention" and Superior Electoral Court President Luís Roberto Barroso commenting that "the \[democratic\] institutions are working". Estadão's editor, João Caminoto, reaffirms the veracity of the report in a social media post.

Source citations (as archived): [G1](<https://g1.globo.com/politica/noticia/2021/07/22/braga-netto-nega-que-tenha-feito-ameaca-contra-as-eleicoes-de-2022.ghtml>).

### 2021-07-23

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1101106965](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2021%20July%2023&oldid=1101106965>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2021-07-23-0-3"></a>

Context: War in Afghanistan / Taliban insurgency / 2021 Taliban offensive.

**Archived source account.** Taliban spokesperson Suhail Shaheen says that the Islamist group "does not want to monopolize" Afghanistan, pointing to past failed attempts by countries to do so. Shaheen also says that women's rights under the Taliban would now be respected, although women would still need to wear a headscarf or hijab and have a male relative as a companion in order to leave their house. Shaheen also accused President Ashraf Ghani of being a "warmonger" and said that "no one wants a civil war in Afghanistan".

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/23/taliban-afghanistan-ashraf-ghani-civil-war>).

<a id="event-2021-07-23-0-5"></a>

Context: Allied Democratic Forces insurgency; 2021 Democratic Republic of the Congo attacks.

**Archived source account.** Gunmen open fire on a civilian convoy that was returning from a weekly market in North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo, killing at least 16 people.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/23/sixteen-civilians-killed-in-eastern-drc-ambush>).

<a id="event-2021-07-23-0-7"></a>

Context: 2021 Armenia–Azerbaijan border crisis.

**Archived source account.** Azerbaijan reports that one of its soldiers was killed by an Armenian sniper in Kalbajar District near the Armenia–Azerbaijan border.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://news.trust.org/item/20210723124345-13j0u/>).

<a id="event-2021-07-23-0-9"></a>

Context: Assassination of Jovenel Moïse.

**Archived source account.** Gunshots are heard at Jovenel Moïse’s funeral, with U.S. Ambassador to the UN Linda Thomas-Greenfield cancelling the remainder of her visit to Haiti as a result of the incident.

Source citations (as archived): [NBC News](<https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/u-s-ambassador-u-n-hastily-leaves-haiti-after-gunshots-n1274852>).

Context: Chikun kidnapping.

**Archived source account.** Nigerian authorities confirm that the bandits who kidnapped dozens of children from a school in Chikun, Kaduna State, have released 28 of them and that 81 others remain in captivity. This was the tenth mass kidnapping incident since December 2020.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/kidnappers-nigeria-release-28-schoolchildren-another-81-still-held-says-2021-07-25/>).

<a id="event-2021-07-25-0-5"></a>

**Archived source account.** Armed bandits kidnap a negotiator who had been sent to pay the ransom by the parents of the remaining students being held in captivity. The bandits had demanded nearly US$73,000.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/nigerian-bandits-abduct-negotiator-over-ransom-free-students-says-school-2021-07-25/>).

<a id="event-2021-07-25-0-7"></a>

Context: Mali War.

**Archived source account.** The man who tried to kill Malian President Assimi Goïta with a knife at a mosque in Bamako six days ago dies in custody. The cause of death is unknown.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/26/man-accused-of-trying-to-kill-mali-president-dies-in-custody>).

<a id="event-2021-07-25-0-9"></a>

Context: Insurgency in Cabo Delgado.

**Archived source account.** Mozambique President Filipe Nyusi reports that the Mozambique Defence Armed Forces are advancing in Cabo Delgado Province and gaining territory previously held by Daesh-affiliated groups. The insurgency has caused thousands of deaths as well as monetary losses Mozambique's economy, primarily in the gas and oil industries.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/mozambique-president-nyusi-says-army-gaining-ground-insurgency-hit-region-2021-07-25/>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2021-07-27-0-1"></a>

Context: Afar–Somali clashes.

**Archived source account.** According to the government of Ethiopia's Somali Region, militants from the Afar Region attack for the fourth day the Somali town of Garbaiisa, killing up to 300 people. In response, protesters set up roadblocks along a highway leading to Djibouti and damaged parts of the Addis Ababa–Djibouti Railway, threatening Ethiopia's economy. This comes after multiple days of fighting between Afar and Somali militants in Garbaiisa.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/hundreds-civilians-killed-attack-ethiopias-somali-region-local-government-says-2021-07-27/>); [Bloomberg](<https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-07-27/protests-block-djibouti-ethiopia-railway-somali-guardian-says>).

<a id="event-2021-07-27-0-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** The Cuban embassy in Paris, France, is attacked with three molotovs, resulting in a fire outside the building but without causing any injuries. The identities of the perpetrators of the attack are unknown.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/27/cuba-says-paris-embassy-targeted-with-petrol-bombs>).

#### Arts and culture

<a id="event-2021-07-27-1-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** The U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York orders American handicraft chain Hobby Lobby to forfeit a 3,600-year-old tablet containing a portion of the Epic of Gilgamesh to the federal government, after the company illegally purchased it in a private auction in 2014. The Justice Department had been looking to claim the tablet since 2013, as it was suspected to have been stolen from an Iraqi archeological site in the aftermath of the 1991 Gulf War, so it could be repatriated back to Iraq.

Source citations (as archived): [CNN](<https://www.cnn.com/2021/07/27/politics/epic-of-gilgamesh-hobby-lobby/index.html>); [NBC News](<https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/politics-news/justice-department-seizes-rare-ancient-tablet-illegally-auctioned-hobby-lobby-n1275217>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2021-07-28-0-3"></a>

Context: War in Afghanistan / Taliban insurgency / 2021 Taliban offensive.

**Archived source account.** U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken says that United Nations reports of civilian deaths in Afghanistan are "deeply, deeply troubling" as the Taliban gains vital border crossings and territory. The armed group has said that, if they return to power, they will treat civilians well and will not allow Afghanistan to be used as a base for international terrorism.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/taliban-attacks-civilians-deeply-troubling-says-blinken-2021-07-28/>).

<a id="event-2021-07-28-0-5"></a>

Context: 2021 Armenia–Azerbaijan border crisis.

**Archived source account.** Armenia reports that three of its soldiers were killed in clashes with Azerbaijani forces in the disputed Nagorno-Karabakh region. Armenia says that Azerbaijan "is deliberately escalating the situation as its forces remain illegally on Armenia's sovereign territory" while Azerbaijan rejects the accusation and blames Armenian forces for opening fire first towards Azerbaijani forces in the district of Kelbajar.

Source citations (as archived): [DW](<https://www.dw.com/en/armenia-says-three-troops-dead-in-clashes-with-azerbaijan/a-58667797>).

<a id="event-2021-07-28-1-0"></a>

Economy minister Martín Guzmán asks both entities to restructure the debts in order to make payment viable. The IMF has expressed its willingness for the payment after months of negotiations on a $45 billion debt acquired by the previous administration.

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2021-07-31-0-3"></a>

Context: War in Afghanistan / Taliban insurgency / 2021 Taliban offensive.

**Archived source account.** Government forces and the Taliban clash in Herat, the provincial capital of Herat Province, where the Islamist group has seized many districts. The Taliban also captures adjoining border crossings with Iran and Turkmenistan as the United Nations accuses them of killing a United Nations serviceman yesterday during an attack on a UN compound.

Source citations (as archived): [France 24](<https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210731-taliban-and-afghan-forces-clash-again-outside-herat-city>).

<a id="event-2021-07-31-0-4"></a>

Context: War in Afghanistan / Taliban insurgency / 2021 Taliban offensive.

**Archived source account.** The Taliban enters Kandahar as intense fighting is reported in three major cities. Kandahar MP spokesman Gul Ahmad Kamin says that the fighting there is the worst that has been seen in 20 years, with the Taliban seeking to establish their temporary capital there. Kamin also says that the situation is worsening "hour by hour" as he warns that if Kandahar falls, five or six other provinces in the region would also be captured by the Taliban. It is also reported that the Taliban made rapid major gains in rural areas.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-58040141>).

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/1/egypt-eight-troops-killed-in-sinai-anti-terrorism-operations>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2021-08-01-0-1"></a>

Context: July 2021 Gulf of Oman incident.

**Archived source account.** The United Kingdom and the United States join Israel in blaming Iran for the strike. British Foreign Secretary Dominic Raab says that the UK and its allies are planning a coordinated response. However, an Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson says the allegation is "baseless."

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<https://apnews.com/article/middle-east-business-iran-persian-gulf-tensions-419efc522acbd213a79696c9876af6dc?repost>); [The Hill](<https://thehill.com/homenews/administration/565845-us-blames-iran-for-attack-on-oil-tanker-off-oman-forwarding-statement>).

<a id="event-2021-08-01-0-4"></a>

Context: Insurgency in the Maghreb / 2021 Niger attacks.

**Archived source account.** Fifteen troops are killed and six others are missing as Islamists ambush them in Torodi, Tillabéri Region, Niger. A bomb also explodes as the soldiers tried to evacuate their wounded.

Source citations (as archived): [France 24](<https://www.france24.com/en/africa/20210801-more-than-a-dozens-soldiers-killed-several-missing-in-niger-attack>).

<a id="event-2021-08-01-0-6"></a>

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/1/six-civilians-killed-several-wounded-in-car-rebel-attack>).

<a id="event-2021-08-01-0-7"></a>

**Archived source account.** Five people, including three Hezbollah members, are killed and several more are wounded as gunmen open fire at the funeral of Ali Shibli, a Hezbollah member who was assassinated yesterday in Khalde, Lebanon. Both the attacks are described as motivated by anti-shi'ism and as a revenge for the killing of a Sunni Arab teenager and a Syrian last year in the same town.

Source citations (as archived): [France 24](<https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210801-three-hezbollah-among-5-dead-in-lebanon-funeral-ambush-security-source>).

#### Arts and culture

<a id="event-2021-08-01-1-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** YouTube bans News Corp's Sky News Australia channel from uploading new content for seven days after commentator Alan Jones spreads COVID-19 misinformation. This comes shortly after The Daily Telegraph fired Jones and ended his regular column over similar concerns. According to a YouTube spokesman, "Specifically, we don’t allow content that denies the existence of Covid-19 or that encourages people to use hydroxychloroquine or ivermectin to treat or prevent the virus."

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/media/2021/aug/01/sky-news-australia-banned-from-youtube-for-seven-days-over-covid-misinformation>).

<a id="event-2021-08-01-1-1"></a>

**Archived source account.** Canada observes "Emancipation Day" nationwide for the first time. The holiday, commemorating the day in 1834 when the Slavery Abolition Act 1833 came into force and outlawed slavery in Canada and most of the British Empire, was unanimously declared by Parliament in March.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/1/canada-marks-first-ever-nationwide-emancipation-day>).

<a id="event-2021-08-01-1-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** New Zealand Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern formally apologizes to the Pacific Islander community for the Dawn Raids, a series of police raids in the 1970s that targeted and deported Pacific Islanders accused of overstaying their work visas, and says that the government will create new education and training scholarships for the community, and an official account of the raids in order to compensate for them. The apology was supposed to happen in June, but it was delayed due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/1/new-zealand-apologizes-for-1970s-dawn-raids>).

**Archived source account.** Spain donates 7.5 million vaccines to Latin American countries, with the first countries to receive these vaccines being Peru, Paraguay and Guatemala.

Source citations (as archived): [Prensa Latina](<https://www.plenglish.com/index.php?o=rn&amp;id=70287&amp;SEO=spain-begins-donation-of-vaccines-to-latin-america>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2021-08-05-3-1"></a>

Context: COVID-19 pandemic in France, COVID-19 vaccination in France.

**Archived source account.** The French Constitutional Council approves most of the controversial measures that would begin on August 9 which include requiring health passes to enter restaurants, cafés, some shopping centres, and use some types of public transportation. The council also approves the vaccine mandate for healthcare workers and other health professionals, in which they must present proof that they have received at least one dose of the vaccine beginning on September 15 and must present proof of full vaccination beginning on October 15. However, judges considered the mandatory 10-day quarantine to be a violation of aspects of French liberties.

Source citations (as archived): [Euronews](<https://www.euronews.com/2021/08/05/french-move-to-require-a-covid-pass-to-access-restaurants-is-approved-by-constitutional-co>).

<a id="event-2021-08-05-3-3"></a>

Context: Protests over responses to the COVID-19 pandemic, COVID-19 pandemic in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.

**Archived source account.** Prime Minister of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines Ralph Gonsalves is injured during protests against changes to the Public Health Act, which includes mandatory vaccination against COVID-19 for public sector workers and those in "frontline jobs". The Prime Minister received treatment for a head wound.

Source citations (as archived): [Caribbean National Weekly](<https://www.caribbeannationalweekly.com/caribbean-breaking-news-featured/st-vincent-prime-minister-injured-during-vaccine-protest/>).

<a id="event-2021-08-05-3-5"></a>

Context: Hong Kong national security law.

**Archived source account.** LGBT organizations and Amnesty International ask Hong Kong to release detained activist Jimmy Sham, who has been repeatedly denied bail since his arrest in February. Amnesty says that Sham has been held in prison "simply for speaking out for his community and LGBTQIA+ rights in Hong Kong." These organizations also warned of Sham's upcoming trial along with 46 others where he could face many more years in prison for "subversion."

Source citations (as archived): [Star Observer](<https://www.starobserver.com.au/news/out-gay-hong-kong-pro-democracy-activist-faces/204938>).

<a id="event-2021-08-05-3-7"></a>

Context: 2021 Ghana gay arrests.

**Archived source account.** A court in Ghana drops a case against 21 LGBT activists who were arrested in May. The 16 women and five men were arrested at a hotel in the Volta Region for an alleged unlawful assembly, of which the court said that there was not enough evidence to prove the charges. The other charges were dismissed, as promoting LGBT rights is not a crime in Ghana.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/ghana-lgbt-idUSL8N2PC6MO>).

<a id="event-2021-08-05-3-8"></a>

**Archived source account.** Six members of a paramilitary force in Sudan are sentenced to death for their involvement in the killing of six people during a 2019 protest in El-Obeid.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/5/sudan-sentences-paramilitaries-to-death-for-killing-protesters>).

Source citations (as archived): [Deutsche Welle](<https://www.dw.com/en/iran-ebrahim-raisi-sworn-in-as-president/a-58771047>).

#### Science and technology

<a id="event-2021-08-05-5-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Apple Inc. announces that it will begin to continuously scan its smartphone and tablet devices for child sexual abuse material (CSAM). Before an image is stored on the iCloud, the new system will search for matches of already known CSAM. The company claims the system has an "extremely high level of accuracy", and will be included in iOS and iPadOS updates later this year.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-58109748>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2021-08-06-0-3"></a>

Context: War in Afghanistan / Taliban insurgency / 2021 Taliban offensive.

**Archived source account.** Dawa Khan Menapal, head of the Government Media and Information Centre, is assassinated in Kabul. The Taliban claims responsibility for the killing, saying that Menapal "was punished for his actions".

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/taliban-says-it-has-killed-afghan-governments-top-media-officer-2021-08-06/>).

<a id="event-2021-08-06-0-4"></a>

Context: War in Afghanistan / Taliban insurgency / 2021 Taliban offensive.

**Archived source account.** The Taliban captures Zaranj, the provincial capital of Nimruz Province, making it the first major capture of a provincial city by the group since the 2001 invasion. A spokesperson for the local police confirms that the city has fallen into Taliban control and blames the lack of reinforcements of military from the central government.

Source citations (as archived): [The West Australia](<https://thewest.com.au/news/conflict/taliban-target-two-provincial-capitals-c-3614411>).

<a id="event-2021-08-06-0-6"></a>

Context: Iran–Israel proxy conflict.

**Archived source account.** Hezbollah fires twenty rockets at northern Israel from Lebanon, its heaviest barrage since the 2006 war and the second firing of rockets in the past week. The Israel Defense Forces respond with artillery attacks.

Source citations (as archived): [The Times of Israel](<https://www.timesofisrael.com/rocket-alert-sirens-sound-in-golan-heights/>); [VOA](<https://www.voanews.com/middle-east/hezbollah-launches-20-rockets-northern-israel-which-responds-artillery>).

<a id="event-2021-08-06-0-7"></a>

Context: Iran–Israel proxy conflict.

**Archived source account.** Lebanese Druze villagers confront the Hezbollah rocket-launch convoy after it fires at Israel, accusing the militant group of endangering them by firing projectiles near civilian houses. The Lebanese Army later confiscates the launcher and arrests four suspects.

Source citations (as archived): [The Times of Israel](<https://www.timesofisrael.com/lebanese-druze-halt-hezbollah-rocket-launcher-convoy-after-attack-on-israel/>); [Reuters](<https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/world/in-rare-challenge-hezbollah-fighters-held-after-rocket-launch/ar-AAN15gU>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2021-08-08-0-2"></a>

Context: Mali War / Mali attacks.

**Archived source account.** At least 51 people are killed as Islamist militants storm three villages in central Mali, near the border with Niger. It is one of the deadliest recent terror attacks in the country against civilians.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/least-51-killed-mali-village-raids-district-official-says-2021-08-09/>).

<a id="event-2021-08-08-0-6"></a>

Context: War in Afghanistan / Taliban insurgency / 2021 Taliban offensive.

**Archived source account.** The Taliban captures the capitals of the Kunduz, Takhar, and Sar-e Pol provinces. In Kunduz, the Taliban seize key government buildings, leaving the government forces only in control of the airport. In Takhar, the Taliban seize Taloqan, and heavy fighting was reported as the Taliban intensifies its offensive in the north. In Sar-e Pol, the Taliban drive government forces out of the main military base.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-58135148>).

<a id="event-2021-08-08-0-8"></a>

Context: Insurgency in Balochistan.

**Archived source account.** Two policemen are killed and 21 more people are wounded as a roadside bombing explode in a street in Quetta, Pakistan, targeting a police mobile van near a hotel.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/9/roadside-blast-kills-two-policemen-in-southwest-pakistan>).

<a id="event-2021-08-08-0-10"></a>

Context: Insurgency in Cabo Delgado.

**Archived source account.** Rwandan and Mozambican forces retake the city of Mocímboa da Praia, the last rebel stronghold in Cabo Delgado Province. Rwanda had sent 1,000 troops to help Mozambique fight the Islamist insurgency that began in 2017.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-58138507>).

Context: COVID-19 pandemic / COVID-19 pandemic in Asia / COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh, COVID-19 vaccination in Bangladesh.

Fiji is now the hardest-hit country in Oceania and is only second in the number of infections in the region, with the most cases being reported in the U.S. state of Hawaii.

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2021-08-08-3-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Tech company Alibaba Group fires multiple senior executives who had silenced an internal complaint of rape and had ordered a social media blackout of the complaint (Chinese: 阿里巴巴员工被性侵案). The case shed light on rape in China and exposed the business culture of forcing female employees to act as hostesses to entertain business clients.

Source citations (as archived): [The New York Times](<https://www.nytimes.com/2021/08/08/business/alibaba-rape-china-metoo.html>).

<a id="event-2021-08-08-3-1"></a>

The Olympic Flag is handed over to the Mayor of Paris Anne Hidalgo in preparation for the 2024 Games.

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2021-08-09-0-2"></a>

Context: Taliban insurgency / 2021 Taliban offensive.

**Archived source account.** The Taliban captures Samangan (Aibak), the provincial capital of Samangan Province, making it the sixth capture of a provincial capital by the Islamist group in the past four days.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/9/taliban-captures-sixth-afghanistan-provincial-capital-official>).

<a id="event-2021-08-09-0-3"></a>

Context: Taliban insurgency / 2021 Taliban offensive.

**Archived source account.** The Afghan National Security Forces launch a counter-offensive, in an attempt to retake Kunduz, which was captured by the Taliban yesterday. Heavy fighting is reported elsewhere in the northern part of the country, where the Islamist group has launched an offensive. Civilians flee Kunduz, trying to reach Kabul as there are conflicting reports as to who is responsible for dozens of civilian casualties.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/afghan-forces-battling-retake-kunduz-taliban-advance-north-2021-08-09/>).

<a id="event-2021-08-09-0-5"></a>

Context: 17 October Revolution.

**Archived source account.** Violence occurs in Lebanon due to the severe fuel shortages that are affecting the country, leaving three people dead.
